tex_content.html:
If $a\in \operatorname {int}\xi $ and $L(\xi )\le 1$, there is a shortest geodesic in $B$ from $a$ to $v$, meeting $\partial B$ only at its endpoints, of length at most $1/2+\delta '$. \end{claim}
Proof

\sketch A boundary path through the nearer endpoint has the stated length. Compactness produces a minimizer. Any additional contact with a side admits a corner shortcut; tangential return to $\xi $ would cut off a disk whose turning is at most $3\pi /2+\delta $ and whose curvature integral is below $\mu $, contrary to Gauss–Bonnet.
